mapped_songs.comment_text:
Blake Voss has the voice of a 80's Dark Angel, that particular quality that made little Goth-girl's hearts skip a beat. His vocals are a superior blending of: A Robert Smith quirky darkness; The depth of the "King of Goth's" with Peter Murphy; And the confident swagger of David Bowie who embodied the pure definition of "kewl" as these men were considered a paragon of perfection. They didn't "try" to sing....!!!! No-way they were just being themselves ― I feel Blake Voss could become today's icon.

The other half of Vandal Moon's duo, stands Jeremy Einsiedler, whose obviously a synth-virtuoso with a mastery of sounds so clearly familiar to myself, yet refreshingly expressed. A younger generation will call this music Dark Retro New-wave, Nu-Romanticism, Dark Synth-wave, or even perhaps Future-wave because of its timeless quality ― For those of us who spent our youth listening to "New-Wave" music for the first time around the block, it's been a desperately needed respite from the shackles of Gangster-Rap, Hip-Hop, and the endlessness vocal gymnastic stylings of R&B, which all began in the 80's but never died. As someone who works within the music industry, Vandal Moon has remembered to use those old analogue synthesizers (which are worth a fortune now), because they have a warmth to the ear without the brashness new synths often have. Voss's vocal overlays are a sublime textural methodology which everyone seemed to have forgotten until Retro New-wave began gaining a foothold, but this isn't like the "Second British Invasion" of the 80's, although Voss has managed to sneak in a very slight Brit-pop flare. It's a particular vocal withholding singers sometimes use as a breathing technique, with an ever so sensitive inhale through the nose.

Even though I dislike comparisons, but if I were forced to make any comparisons, then they have every-bit of a special brew of the Information Society, Modern English, The Cure, Human League, Echo and the Bunnymen, New Order, Clan of Xymox and so many more that would overwhelm this mini-review. I sincerely hope Vandal Moon is prepared for a multi-generational following which would ring so true when on tour ― Newbie Dark Synth-Wave, Retro New-wave, and even some Kewl Goth-kyds (both youthful and the elder-statesmen) will be standing in the same queue as Mom and Dad, as well as perhaps your Grand-mother and Grand-father (if you started your family early) but in any case kids, forget them dropping you off at the curbside.

Prepare for an ocean of people dressed in all black, except some may naturally have salt-and-pepper color hair. It's a good thing I still have my steel-toe combat-boots just for these occasions. This could be the start of something, that our global community has never seen before, a fully Multi-Generational Cross-Cultural Live Audience (MG-CC-LA) attending Vandal Moon concerts. This is quite the eye-opener for a completely new millennium.
